 The Utah Utes take on the Dayton Flyers in Charleston, SC for the Charleston Classic. Tip-off is set for 5:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Utah is favored by 1.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -115. The total is set at 141.5 points.
 Here's my Utah vs. Dayton prediction and college basketball picks for November 20, 2026.
 Utah vs Dayton Prediction
 Pick: Dayton ML -104 
 My Utah vs Dayton best bet is on the Flyers to win outright. Be sure to find the best lines by using our live NCAAB odds page and download the Action Network app for the latest picks and analysis.
 Utah vs Dayton Odds
 Utah vs Dayton spread: Utah -1.5 (-104), Dayton +1.5 (-118)
 Utah vs Dayton over/under: 141.5 (-110o / -110o)
 Utah vs Dayton moneyline: Utah -115, Dayton -104
 Utah vs Dayton College Basketball Preview
 It's been a tough start for the Utes. They might be 3-1, but their one loss came this week to Eastern Washington . Plus, the Utes trailed in the second half against Weber State and Long Beach State and have covered in just one of their four matchups.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Am I surprised Utah is bad? No, but this is another level. Lacking talent is one thing; barely beating middling mid-majors projected to finish near the bottom of their leagues is another.
 Despite attempting 3s on 45% of their field goals, they make just 25% of them. Every player with 10+ 3s attempted is shooting below 26%. Plus, Utah is giving the ball away at a 21.7% rate. Neither of those is conducive to winning basketball.
 Three players on Utah's roster average 10+ points per game: German freshman Alec Anigbata leads the way with 15 points, while Jackson Holcombe and Trey Campbell are also in double digits. Campbell shot just 33% from 3 last season at Northern Iowa , and Holcombe shot 15% from 3 at Utah Valley.
 The key for Alex Jensen's squad? Defense. If the Utes become a top-50-ish defense, that'll help. They sit at 64th in defensive efficiency right now, per KenPom. They hold foes to 47% shooting on 2s and give up offensive boards just 23% of the time.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Dayton likely owns the crown for the most disappointing team in the country award so far. The Flyers lost back-to-back games as double-digit favorites to Siena and Northern Illinois, before losing by 23 to Cincinnati .
 The Flyers bounced back with a win over Central Michigan, 88-63. Can that win give Dayton the momentum?
 Dayton's offense is more built around inside scoring, shooting 62% on 2-pointers (19th). The duo of 7-footer Amael L'Etang and star freshman Aidan Derkack lead the interior scoring attack.
 Derkack leads the Flyers with 18.6 points per game and shoots a dazzling 67% from the field. Meanwhile, L'Etang does his work both on the perimeter and interior.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Anthony Grant will use him as an offensive hub at times. He averages 15.8 points with 6.0 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game, while shooting 63% from the field and 30% from the 3-point line.
 It's not like Dayton is Utah-level bad at shooting from deep, either. So, why are the Flyers a woeful 105th in offensive efficiency? An 18% turnover rate is a big culprit. Plus, they have a very low 29% offensive rebound rate. So, if the first shot is off, that's usually Dayton's only shot.
 On the other end, Dayton is 139th in defensive efficiency. The Flyers haven't found their DNA on that end, as they rank 151st in 2-point defense, 201st in 3-point defense and give up offensive rebounds 33% of the time.
 If you dive deeper into Dayton's defense in the shocking Siena and Northern Illinois losses, one thing stands out — both teams attempted 30+ free throws. Dayton has to avoid giving teams free points since it already has a bad defense.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Dayton enters as a slight underdog, which is fair. There's nothing the Flyers have done to be favored against a high-major team, even one as bad as Utah.
 Still, I feel better about Dayton turning things around than Utah. It just feels as though Utah is flawed in its approach. The Utes don't have shooters, but they insist on shooting a bunch of 3s. If that doesn't change, the Utes could end up as the worst Power-Four team.
 So, this is more of a Utah fade than Dayton backing, but the Flyers have a better chance to get right.
 Pick: Dayton ML -104
